# fallfloor enterprise

> A reference design (a modelled company, not a client) for running a 1,200-person UK bank's AI on machines it owns: staff laptops as WebGPU nodes plus a small rack of on-premises inference nodes, joined peer to peer, every step signed. It gives the architecture, capacity, a five-year cost comparison against the corporate model (seats plus cloud APIs) with every price sourced and dated, a GDPR / UK GDPR / EU AI Act compliance map quoting the primary law, a sealed dual-map go/no-go board built from fallfloor's receipted evidence, the operating model and the rollout.

- Live page: https://sjgant80-hub.github.io/fallfloor-enterprise/
- Source: https://github.com/sjgant80-hub/fallfloor-enterprise
- Evidence it stands on: https://sjgant80-hub.github.io/fallfloor/
- Prices and their sources: https://github.com/sjgant80-hub/fallfloor-enterprise/blob/main/sources/prices.json
- The law, quoted and dated: https://github.com/sjgant80-hub/fallfloor-enterprise/blob/main/sources/law.json

## Facts

- EU AI Act high-risk (Annex III) duties apply from 2 December 2027 and Annex I from 2 August 2028 (Art 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, the Digital Omnibus on AI, in force 27 July 2026). Article 50 transparency applies from 2 August 2026; AI literacy (Art 4, as replaced) from 2 February 2025.
- UK: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 data protection provisions, including new UK GDPR Articles 22A–22D and the transfer provisions, in force 5 February 2026 (SI 2026/82).
- A company that builds an AI system for its own use is its provider under the AI Act (Art 3(3), 3(11)).
- Local-first removes, for inference, the AI processor (GDPR Art 28) and international transfers (Chapter V); lawful basis, DPIA, accuracy, security and individuals' rights stay with the company.

## Headline

<!-- ⟦RESULTS-BEGIN⟧ generated by tools/make-page.mjs — do not edit here -->
For the modelled bank (1,200 staff, 1,000 knowledge workers, UK with EU customers), over five years, cash, net of VAT:

| | Local-first | Corporate (1,000 × Microsoft 365 Copilot (enterprise) + OpenAI gpt-5-mini) |
|---|---|---|
| 5-year total | £2,073,772 | £2,638,202 |
| People (the largest line on both sides) | £1,872,140 | £1,119,242 |
| Seat licences | — | £1,386,000 |
| Core inference nodes (bought as demand grows, replaced every 4 years) | £87,068 | — |
| Electricity for the AI work (upper bound) | £34,565 | in the vendor's price |
| Share of the total resting on estimates or assumptions | 95.8% | 47.2% |

What has to be true: local-first costs less once more than 59.3% of knowledge workers would otherwise get a seat; below that, the corporate model costs less.

Difference: £564,429 over five years in local-first's favour, ahead from year 1. The corporate side buys frontier-model quality that the local side does not claim.

Compliance (customer-support triage, local-first vs a cloud API, as of 2026-09-29): local-first **removes** processor contracts and due diligence (Art 28(1)) and transfers outside the UK / EEA (EU Art 44; UK Chapter V as amended by DUAA 2025 s.85 and Sch 7 (in force 5 Feb 2026)) for inference; it **keeps with the company** 8 duties, including a lawful basis, a DPIA, accuracy, security and the AI Act provider duties for systems it builds. EU AI Act high-risk (Annex III) duties apply from 2 December 2027 after the Digital Omnibus (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744); Article 50 transparency has applied since 2 August 2026.

Go / no-go board, sealed from fallfloor's receipted evidence: 2 PASS · 2 BLOCK · 3 PENDING (support-unsupervised BLOCK, support-assisted PENDING, screening-auto BLOCK, screening-review PENDING, hr-routing PASS, floor-async PASS, credit-decisions PENDING).
